actionable_steps: Size the pool before searching: require >=2,000 M dwarfs (expect ~150 transiting 1-4 Re planets with P<50 d, ~50 with Rp>2 Re before completeness) and prefer stars where the minimum detectable radius (Sect. 2.5 table) is <=1.5 Re at P 10-30 d, i.e. Kepler/KBONUS G<17.5, K2 Kp<15, TESS T<13 with >=4 sectors.

If staying in KBONUS: reproduce the 1,836-star funnel with kbonus_funnel.py (code in scratchpad), then widen it (PSFFRAC>0.5, CROWDSAP>0.7, >=4 quarters gives 2,379; dropping CROWDSAP to 0.5 or including the 2,040 Kepler-target M dwarfs' PSF light curves adds more) and prioritise the ~130 background stars with G<17; treat G>18 sources as unvettable.

Add a noise-vs-magnitude pre-filter: compute 6-h CDPP per star and flag anything below 0.5x or above 3x the DR25 cool-dwarf median at its G (dl/dr25_cool_dwarfs.csv); low outliers are neighbour-dominated PSF fluxes, high outliers are variables that will dominate false alarms.

Build the period grid yourself (N = OS x baseline/min_duration x ln(Pmax/Pmin); OS 2-3) and never call BoxLeastSquares.autoperiod on multi-year baselines; budget ~1-2 CPU-min per Kepler-length star for BLS, 3-6 s per TESS 2-4 sector star, and double it for the mandatory inverted run.

Calibrate significance empirically: run the identical pipeline (detrending, holdout split, vetting) on inverted and >=38 scrambled copies of every star; report the maximum null score, the per-star pass rate at the candidate's thresholds, and the implied expected number of null events in the search; do not promote a candidate whose score is exceeded by any null star, and size the null at >=10x the search to quote per-star FARs below 1e-3.
Use SNR>=9 with pixel-level localisation as the floor (eumemic's inverted calibration shows ~25% false alarms among SNR>=9 survivors and ~79% at SNR 7.5-9 even after vetting flags).

For TESS pools, target the gaps: 13.5<T<15 M dwarfs within 100 pc (44,639 stars at T 14-15, 6 known TOIs), P 20-50 d with >=6 sectors, and stars with no SPOC/QLP light curve; cross-check every survivor against TOI, CTOI (ExoFOP), TCE and LEO-Vetter outputs before claiming novelty.

Decide the end state in advance from host magnitude and distance: T<13 within 50 pc -> CTOI submission and TFOP SG1 photometry (1-m class), speckle, TRICERATOPS FPP<0.015; Kp>15 Kepler-field -> candidate evidence pack (Zenodo DOI, GitHub, per-quarter depth-vs-aperture-share, raw-TPF centroids, neighbour light curves, injection-recovery, inverted/scrambled nulls) and at most an RNAAS note.

Download from bulk bundles or parallelise MAST fetches (lightkurve took ~30 s per KBONUS star here); plan ~8.5 MB per KBONUS star, 0.47 MB per Kepler quarter, 1.1 MB per TESS-SPOC sector, 10-50 MB per TESScut sector for vetting only.

Report yields honestly: quote the model's detectable count, the empirical 0.36 Kepler known/model ratio as the realism factor, and the measured null pass rates, rather than extrapolated FAPs (both Chopra and Kuber withdrew extrapolated false-alarm figures).
open_questions: How many of the 1,836 (or 27,760) KBONUS 'M stars' are genuine M dwarfs versus reddened distant K dwarfs/giants? The catalogue is colour-selected (Martinez-Palomera+2023 Sect. III.2); a Gaia parallax/absolute-magnitude cut would sharpen the occurrence prior and the yield (not done here).

What fraction of KBONUS background PSF light curves are neighbour-dominated (the 0.23-0.36 noise-ratio cases)? A systematic CDPP-vs-G scan of all 1,836 eligible stars (~4 h of downloads) would quantify it and define a contamination pre-filter.
Actual TESS sector-count distribution for GCNS M dwarfs after Sector 109 (I used 2/4/8-sector scenarios); a tess-point run over the GCNS sample would replace the scenario with a measured histogram.

The realism factor 0.36 (Kepler known/model) mixes pipeline incompleteness, Robovetter losses, catalogue incompleteness and host-Teff crossmatch issues; its transferability to TESS/K2/KBONUS is an assumption worth testing with eumemic's published candidate yields per star searched.
Which K2 M-dwarf samples have already been searched end-to-end (Dressing+2017/2019, Hardegree-Ullman+2020, Zink+2021) and down to what SNR? Without this the K2 'remaining ~200' is an upper bound.

Kuber's two inverted stars at candidate strength (KIC 8701308, KIC 5283912): what are they physically (flare-like systematics, eclipsing binaries, roll-tweak artefacts)? If they would fail his later astrophysical tests, the inverted-null rate at candidate strength overstates the risk for the real candidate; if not, it does not.

Whether the editor's RNAAS objections (sample construction, other search outcomes, TESS non-detection, Barber et al. 2022 catalogue match) can be met with existing data, or whether new ground-based photometry (2-m class, ~5 transit windows per year from a northern site) is the only route to a publishable result for KIC 5689121.

Current QLP/SPOC faint-star FFI search limits in the second and third extended missions (T<13.5 is documented for the primary and first extended mission); if official searches now reach T~14-15, the TESS 'unsearched' residual shrinks.
